strings: Wizzle Brassbolts is an Alliance gnome engineer stationed alongside his fellow tinkerers out on the salt flats of Thousand Needles. Working with the gnomish racing team at the Mirage Raceway, he seeks durable local materials to reinforce their experimental rocket cars.

Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between gnomish and goblin engineering takes the form of high-speed rocket car races. Wizzle Brassbolts works as part of the gnomish raceway crew, striving to keep their vehicles intact against blistering speeds and abrasive salt. To bolster their machines, he recruits adventurers to hunt the local wildlife—such as the sturdy turtles wandering the basin—harvesting thick shells and natural plating to reinforce the team's chassis.

Wizzle maintains close ties with friends across the continents, including fellow tinkerers and aerial scouts like Pilot Longbeard. Whether trading supplies, sharing schematics, or sending couriers back and forth with custom-machined parts, Wizzle keeps the gnomish team supplied despite their remote, inhospitable testing ground on the Shimmering Flats.

Wizzlecrank's Shredder is a lumber machine stranded in the foul depths of Sludge Fen in the northern Barrens. Operated by the gnome Pilot Wizzlecrank, the battered mechanical walker sits disabled amidst hostile Venture Company operators. Helping fire up its engine is the only way the trapped pilot can make a desperate bid for freedom.

Deep within the oil-slicked, heavily polluted basin of Sludge Fen sits Wizzlecrank's Shredder, immobile and surrounded by hostile Venture Company mercenaries. The pilot inside, a gnome named Wizzlecrank, found himself cut off and trapped when the machine stalled out during his excursion into the drilling compound. Unable to open the cockpit safely amid hostile guards and mechanical overseers, the pilot remains sealed inside, frantically trying to bypass the ignition systems before the Venture Company decides to scrap the machine with him in it.

Once provided with an alternate ignition key salvaged from the Venture Company supervisors patrolling the oil pools, the shredder clatters violently back to life. With its whirling blades and heavy metal plating, Pilot Wizzlecrank uses the lumbering contraption to batter through the enclosing mercenary defenses, relying on sympathetic passersby to escort the vulnerable contraption up out of the basin to safety.
The mechanical walker is piloted by Pilot Wizzlecrank, an intrepid gnome engineer who ended up stranded right in the middle of Venture Company territory when his machine broke down.

Wynne Larson is a human clothier and robe merchant operating in Stormwind City's Mage Quarter. With the historic arcane textile centers of Dalaran and Quel'Thalas ruined in the Third War, she relies on local craftsmen to supply mages across the kingdom. She regularly directs adventuring spellcasters toward the rare materials required to craft powerful enchanted garments.

Before the Third War, the finest woven fabrics and enchanted vestments came from the magical workshops of Dalaran and the high elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas. The destruction of both northern realms crippled traditional trade routes and devastated arcane textile production. Vendors like Wynne Larson in Stormwind's Mage Quarter have had to adapt, coordinating directly with local tailors and enchanters like Lucan Cordell to meet the city's growing demand for robes and spellwoven gear.

Novice and journeyman mages seeking garments imbued with arcane potency often find their way to Wynne's shop. She knows precisely what materials are required to tailor vestments like Manaweave Robes or Astral Knot Garments, often sending practitioners of the arcane into dangerous territories to recover exotic reagents such as pristine spider silk. Her efforts ensure that Stormwind's practitioners remain properly outfitted despite northern shortages.

Yeh'kinya is a jungle troll scholar residing at Steamwheedle Port on the desert coast of Tanaris. Claiming to seek ancient lore and artifacts to understand dark powers, he dispatches willing adventurers across Azeroth on missions to gather lost troll relics.

Lounging among the goblins and dockworkers of Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya presents himself as a quiet student of history and spirits. He recruits travelers to track down obscure magical items across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, from ancient eggs in the Hinterlands to stone prophecy tablets buried in the ruins of Zul'Farrak. While he claims these errands serve peaceful academic inquiry into ancient troll history, his specific focus on the blood god Hakkar draws suspicion from watchful onlookers.

Beneath his scholarly guise, Yeh'kinya is a fanatical worshipper of Hakkar the Soulflayer. Every artifact and soul essence he gathers is carefully manipulated to prepare for the dread Blood God's physical rebirth into Azeroth. Once his plot is pieced together and exposed by Prospector Ironboot, Yeh'kinya sheds all pretense of friendship. Rather than answering for his treason, he transforms into a green wind serpent and flees across the open sea toward the south seas, leaving duped heroes to seek aid from the Zandalari on Yojamba Isle.

Yvette Farthing is a Forsaken resident of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, dwelling in the Gallows' End Tavern alongside her father, Coleman. Though she appears as hardened and detached as any of Sylvanas's people, she carries the lingering ghost of a mortal romance cut short by the Scourge.

Before the Third War swept Lordaeron into ruin, Yvette was in love with Thurman Agamand, one of the heirs of the prosperous Agamand Mills. When the Scourge plague approached, Yvette and her father, Coleman, begged Thurman to abandon the estate and flee with them. Thurman refused out of devotion to his family's legacy. Both would eventually perish and rise into undeath, but while Yvette found a place among the free-willed Forsaken in Brill, Thurman's tragic final fate remained unknown to her.

Before the mills were overrun, Thurman penned an urgent love letter to Yvette, detailing the treachery of his brother Devlin and lamenting his choice to stay. The Scourge intercepted the message, leaving it lost among the ruins of Agamand Mills until recovered by adventurers. Upon reading Thurman's dying confession, Yvette briefly displays genuine mortal despair before forcing herself back into cold detachment, bitter that such past attachments have no place in the grim reality of the Forsaken.

Zardeth of the Black Claw is a warlock dwelling in the dim subterranean chambers beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Operating under the guise of an unassuming patron, he coordinates covert measures to protect the city's hidden warlock cabal from outside scrutiny. When inquisitive nobles begin looking too closely into their activities, Zardeth ensures those inquiries end permanently.

While the Mage Quarter's towering spires study arcane discipline in the open, the underground tunnels beneath the Slaughtered Lamb house those who traffic in darker arts. Zardeth of the Black Claw operates from these crypts, functioning as a watchful guardian for the practitioners hiding right beneath the city guard's nose. Because the Alliance officially condemns fel magic, survival requires an ironclad secret and a willingness to eliminate any threat before royal investigators come knocking.

When Lord Baurles K. Wishock discovered whispers of the hidden warlock coven, the nobleman began lobbying the House of Nobles for an immediate, full-scale investigation. Aware that such scrutiny would destroy their underground haven, Zardeth arranged a clandestine countermeasure. Capitalizing on the lord's known indulgence in fine liquor, Zardeth dispatched an operative across the eastern kingdoms to gather rare, lethal flora—the Tear of Tilloa from Duskwood and Musquash Root from beneath the Stonewrought Dam.

Blending the gathered reagents with stout ale, Zardeth concocted the Black Claw Stout, a lethal vintage engineered to look like an ordinary luxury gift. Once delivered to Wishock's estate, the poisoned brew did its work swiftly and quietly.
